newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian PM wants probe of Norilsk sale.
newsitem.headline: Russian PM wants probe of Norilsk sale.

text.p: Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin has dropped his last-minute objection to the sale of a big stake in the Norilsk Nickel metals group but still wants a probe of the controversial auction, Prime-Tass news agency said on Wednesday.

It quoted a government source as saying Chernomyrdin wanted an investigation, probably by the Prosecutor-General's office, into whether the investment tender for the huge metals company had contravened Russian law.
The fact that Chernomyrdin had dropped his objection to the auction did not mean he had changed his mind about the need for an investigation into the legality of the sale, Tass said.
It did not say on what grounds the prime minister thought the sale had violated the law.

Svift, a company representing the interests of powerful commercial bank Uneximbank, won the auction for the 38 percent stake in mining and metals group Norilsk on Tuesday by bidding the equivalent of around $250 million.
Svift must also invest $300 million in a gas deposit which will be used to fuel RAO Norilsky Nikel's main metals combine, and pay off company debts of around $70 million.

Uneximbank has been at the centre of a brewing controversy over Russia's murky privatisation process since leading a consortium which won a quarter stake in the Svyazinvest telecoms holding late last month.
